title: Student Data Bridge & Exposure Architecture
verdictDetail: Design complete. No operational student data exists in the repository.

structural.description: Client-side learner state management. Tracks current session: hints consumed, confidence ratings, question responses. Stored in browser localStorage/memory. Not persisted server-side.
structural.notes: Operational at runtime but no export mechanism. Would require explicit export action or server-side logging to populate student database.

structural.description: S252 Board H script. Consumes student_roll.json and student_exports/ directory. Produces student_exposure.json with per-student question exposure, duplicate detection, and challenge linkage.
structural.notes: Script is complete and operational, but has no data to consume.

structural.description: Case study content with scoring rubrics. Contains answer keys and distractor explanations. Not student performance data — these are content files, not student records.
structural.notes: Scoring logic exists but no student attempt records are stored.

structural.description: Application layer with hint tracking, exam-mode gate, and defect-aware recommendations. Tracks per-session statistics but does not persist student records across sessions.
structural.notes: Coaching layer tracks per-attempt data at runtime. Cross-session student record requires export/persistence mechanism.

aspirational.description: 35 synthetic seed challenges. Self-identifies as 'synthetic seed data for development and testing.'
aspirational.notes: Real student challenge data would replace this in production.

import.schema: StudentBatchImport: array of student records with embedded attempts, exposures, results
validationRules: Every qid must exist in question_history.json
Every sessionId must exist in session_registry.json (if provided)
studentId must be unique within the batch
attemptId must be unique within the batch
selectedChoice must be A/B/C/D or null
import.errorHandling: Row-level rejection with error detail. Valid rows committed, invalid rows rejected with reason.

queries: Student performance by domain (avg score, attempt count per domain A-F)
Question exposure frequency (how many students saw each QID)
Most challenging questions (highest incorrect rate per QID)
Student challenge history (all challenges per student)
Attempt timeline (all attempts ordered by time per student)

apiContract.lookupStudent: Input: studentId → Output: student record + all attempts + exposures + results + challenges
apiContract.lookupQuestionExposure: Input: qid → Output: exposure count, correct/incorrect distribution, avg time, avg hints
apiContract.lookupDomainPerformance: Input: domain (A-F), cohortId (optional) → Output: aggregate score stats per domain
apiContract.lookupChallengeHistory: Input: studentId or qid → Output: all related challenges with status

pii: studentId (if linked to real identity elsewhere)
export files containing timestamps that could identify individuals

accessControls.admin: Full access to all student records and aggregate analytics
accessControls.instructor: Access to cohort-level aggregate data + individual student records within their cohort
accessControls.student: Access to own records only (self-service dashboard)
accessControls.system: Read-only access for pipeline automation, no export

retentionPolicy.attemptData: Retained for duration of program + 12 months post-completion
retentionPolicy.challengeData: Retained indefinitely (anonymized — part of content quality record)

governanceIntegration.connection: Student data ingestion triggers governance-guard Rule 4 verification (answer-key changes must include re-verified note). Student challenges feed into defect detection pipeline (→ REC-IDs → investigation_registry).
governanceIntegration.rules: No new governance rules needed. Existing Rules 1-6 cover certification, registry, and defect enforcement for content. Student data is operational analytics, not content modification.

decision.rationale: The canonical student record schema is fully designed with field-level types, constraints, and foreign key relationships to all existing registries (question_history, session_registry, challenge_registry). Import/export contracts specify formats, validation rules, and API query signatures. Privacy and governance controls are defined across all 4 dimensions (classification, access, retention, integration). However, zero operational student data exists in the repository. The student_exposure_index.js script is complete and validated but has no data to consume. The data bridge is architecturally ready but cannot be operationally validated until real student data is available.
